history: As per GE imageries, initiation of the landslide in the source area occurred during the monsoon of 2018. During the successive years, the area of the slide seems increasing and also observed minor slides developed along both the flanks of the stream. The present debris flow occurred at 1:00 AM on 30.07.2024
landuse: High Height Plantation, Low Height Plantation and Settlement
communication: Roads, bridges and transmission lines damaged. Bridge connecting Mundakkai to Chooralmala washed away.
geoscientific_causes: The excessive rainfall is the major triggering factor which results in increase of pore water pressure and reduction of strength on super saturation initiated the slide. Toe erosion by stream.
remedial: Detailed scientific study has to carried out for proposing proper remedial measures
source_report: GSI PDLS 2024, Post-Disaster Studies of Landslides in Kerala, 2024

geomorphology: Located on the northern foot slope of an E -W trending rocky ridge having general elevation of +1000 -1050m above msl. The ridge is lowly dissected and raises steeply ~100m from the surrounding levels. However, the overburden laden foot slope is moderately sloping with less dissections.
lithology: Hornblende-biotite gneiss is exposed on the ridge as well as on the stream beds. However, the failed cut slope comprises of residual soil developed over highly weathered bedrock.
geoscientific_causes: Steep unprotected cut taken in residual soil for road construction. Heavy rainfall resulted in the pore water pressure increment within the relatively thick overburden, leading to subsequent loss of shear strength and failure.
remedial: Removal of the high head trees along the brim of the cut slope as they add head load; in addition, proper toe support is recommended. The lined side drain, which is under construction, may be extended to this reach.
source_report: GSI PDLS 2025, Post-Disaster Studies of Landslides in Kerala, 2025
